description: We are a team of CS engineering freshers taking on the NASA Space Apps challenge "Field Shift: Adapting Farms with NASA Data". We're building a simple web dashboard using NASA POWER data (rainfall, temperature) to give farmers easy crop and irrigation advice. Looking for teammates with web development, data analysis, agriculture, Earth science, or video/pitch skills. Beginners welcome!
summary: FIELDWISE ("From orbit to every field") is an interactive, bilingual (English and Kannada) decision-support dashboard designed to help Bengaluru farmers plan sustainable crop rotations—specifically evaluating the Ragi (Kharif) to Horse Gram (Rabi) cycle. By integrating NASA Earth observation datasets (NASA POWER climate data, HLS/Landsat NDVI, and NASA Worldview) with local agronomic knowledge, FIELDWISE translates complex satellite metrics into an instant, actionable Crop Rotation Suitability Score. Farmers and agricultural officers can adjust real-time "What-If" climate sliders (rainfall and temperature shifts) alongside personal priorities like water saving, yield, risk tolerance, and soil health. The platform visualizes seasonal rainfall against crop water needs, root-zone soil moisture, heat stress risks, and optimal sowing windows, while allowing users to export downloadable CSV reports. FIELDWISE bridges the gap between raw space data and grassroots farming to build climate-resilient agriculture.
details:
FIELDWISE is a climate-and-soil decision-support web app that helps smallholder farmers in Bengaluru evaluate crop rotation strategies using real satellite and ground data — directly from NASA's POWER API and Earth observation systems.

What it does: FIELDWISE analyzes one optimal rotation — Ragi (Kharif, Jun–Oct) → Horse Gram (Rabi, Nov–Feb) — and scores its viability (0–100) based on four pillars: rainfall adequacy, heat stress, soil moisture, and sowing-window timing. Farmers get a plain-language verdict ("Good", "Caution", "Risky"), actionable strategies, and downloadable reports — in both English and Kannada.

How it works: The app runs a 4-tier data pipeline — it first pulls real NASA POWER daily climate data for Bengaluru (2026), then derives soil moisture from precipitation balance, estimates NDVI from temperature/moisture proxies, and falls back to historical averages only when live data is unavailable. A weighted scoring model combines all signals into one recommendation with confidence percentage.

Tools & Stack: Python 3.13, Streamlit, NASA POWER API (MERRA-2 reanalysis), Plotly for interactive charts, Pandas/NumPy for data processing. Frontend design inspired by AgriOrbit design system (cream-paper UI, dark orbit hero banner, Fraunces + Manrope fonts).

Impact: Bridges the "last mile" gap between satellite data and field decisions for farmers with no GIS expertise. Fully offline-capable with cached NASA data, supports regional language (Kannada), and runs on any browser — no app install needed.

Creative factor: We combined NASA's orbital data with ground-level agronomic knowledge to give farmers a single trust score they can act on immediately — moving from "orbit to every field."
